title: Disk file store symlinks can expose files outside the store to link holders
summary: With --file-store disk, a lower-privileged local user able to modify the store can replace a blob or shard directory with a symlink; a normal download may then read an outside file using server filesystem permissions. A valid stored-file metadata entry is also required, obtainable by multi-view upload when uploads are enabled. HTTP-only attackers cannot plant the symlink; database and S3 backends are unaffected.
ai_role: The Yopass maintainer's case-specific security advisory explicitly credits Anthropic's OSS Scanner as discoverer (tracking identifier ANT-2026-3S1O398V). It does not name a model version or internal discovery date.
classification_note: The public maintainer advisory documents the finding; it does not establish whether defenders knew of it or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: Yopass 16.0.0 fixes the issue (commit aabb02807a73d772dd8891212c2152a66d7e2a9b). Affected-version scope: Disk file storage versions 14.0.0 through 15.1.0; fixed in 16.0.0. Fix uses Go os.Root for confined operations and refuses non-regular download files. Patch availability does not establish downstream deployment.

impacts.conditions: A local store-directory writer can cause downloads to read server-readable files outside the store, potentially including credentials or private files.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a possible or reproducible trigger as stated; it does not report observed exploitation in the wild.
